# About this Group Meeting {.unnumbered}

**MetaScience, Scientific Inquiry, and Agents**  
Denolle Lab research-group pilot  
**Thirteen one-hour meetings, taken one at a time**

## Purpose

Reconstruct how experimental, observational, historical, and theoretical research actually proceeds, then translate those lessons into scientifically grounded agent designs and evaluations. The adequacy of a hypothesis-generation/testing loop is a question to investigate, not a conclusion the seminar assumes.

One proposal runs alongside the rest: that agents for science let a researcher work competently across more fields, making individual polymathy practical again. It is an open question here. [Meeting 11](sessions/11-polymathy.qmd) states the hypothesis, the historical evidence bearing on it, and the observations that would count against it.

Start with the [glossary](glossary.qmd). It gives working definitions of the modes of inquiry and of the terms the quarter measures, field-shaping, novelty, depth, interdisciplinarity, and impact, and meeting 1 revises it. This is an exploratory quarter for the group. Nothing here is a settled syllabus, and the [bibliography](bibliography.qmd) is meant to grow. [How to contribute](contributing.qmd) covers adding a note, a reading, or a correction.

## How the paper pairings work

Each meeting uses two scholarly papers with a specific relationship: argument/counterpoint, discovery/diagnostic scrutiny, capability/calibration, or practice/framework. A pairing is not necessarily a disagreement. Read the assigned portions; rotating discussants read both in depth. No participant is expected to read every optional extension.

Meetings 1, 6, 9, and 13 also carry discussant-led papers: the full-length version of Cleland's argument in meeting 1, Ioannidis on false findings in meeting 6, Geller on earthquake prediction in meeting 9, and the two critiques in meeting 13, which merges what were previously separate architecture and evaluation meetings. Each is taken in depth by one rotating discussant; everyone else reads the abstract. The reading load stays at two papers per participant throughout.

For each paper distinguish its scientific claim, the evidence offered, its limits, and the evidence it provides about the research process. A philosophical argument, a retrospective autobiography, an archival history, a primary research report, and a benchmark paper are not interchangeable records of actual practice. Where chronology is not documented, label reconstruction as inference.

## Standing questions

1. What was known at the beginning, and what was the initial question?
2. Which observation, representation, instrument, or model changed the next action?
3. When did the eventual hypothesis appear, and what was exploratory or confirmatory?
4. Where did surprise, failed expectation, opportunism, or missing evidence matter?
5. What is documented about the trajectory, and what disappears from the publication narrative?
6. Which action could an agent perform, and how would we know it had performed it well?

## Quarter outputs

The group develops an inquiry-action vocabulary, exploration policy, trace-inference worksheet, measurement-provenance checklist, adaptive observation plan, Novelty Dossier, Polymathy Profile, Scientific Advance Profile, and finally an agent architecture and evaluation protocol produced together, as a change list against the group's own agent family and suites in its evaluation vault. Across meetings 1 to 9 it also keeps an [inquiry-mode ledger](rubrics.qmd#inquiry-mode-ledger), one row per reconstructed episode, so that the question of where a hypothesis gate would have helped is answered case by case rather than by impression. In parallel it can run the [corpus study](corpus-study.qmd), which codes the mode of inquiry of published papers with the glossary as codebook and relates mode to impact, novelty, interdisciplinarity, and depth, so that the nine hand-reconstructed cases have a counterpart at scale. The [design notes](agent-design.qmd) carry what the readings give an agent designer forward into meeting 13. The [working rubrics](rubrics.qmd) are design proposals to revise, not validated scales.

Before specifying any agent, consult the [prior art](prior-art.qmd) chapter: it catalogues the systems and benchmarks that already exist and, for each, what its scores do not establish. The point of building anything here is to add to that record rather than repeat it.

## Reading access and public use

Every assigned paper has a DOI, publisher, repository, or official proceedings link. Some full texts require institutional access. This book does not redistribute journal PDFs or claim that freely readable papers may automatically be republished. Use the publisher’s download link or institutional library for personal reading, and check the license before putting third-party files on the public site.

The [bibliography](bibliography.qmd) collects every reading by meeting, with links and access notes, the readings the group adds during the quarter, and the full reference list generated from a reusable BibTeX file.

## Version and scope

Working curriculum v0.3, revised September 5, 2026. The reading audit replaces indirect or underspecified pairings with focused cases, adds implemented agents and benchmarks, and separates required pairs from optional extensions. v0.3 merges the former architecture and evaluation meetings into meeting 13 and adds meeting 12 on scientific polymathy; see the [reading audit](https://github.com/Denolle-Lab/metascience-and-AI/blob/main/READING-AUDIT.md) for the rationale. The optional extensions were expanded on September 6, 2026, after a [plan audit](https://github.com/Denolle-Lab/metascience-and-AI/blob/main/PLAN-AUDIT.md); the required pairs did not change. Current evidence does not establish that one architecture is best for all scientific inquiry.
